key_insight: A shallow neural Ritz method can efficiently solve 1D nonlinear diffusion-reaction and Allen-Cahn equations with linear-in-neuron computational cost while preserving accuracy and stability.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable physics-informed alternative to finite elements for stiff nonlinear PDEs, especially when boundary/interior layers must be resolved on fixed meshes.
method: Extend shallow Ritz to cubic nonlinear diffusion-reaction.
Use a reduced block Newton solver with O(n) cost in 1D.
Combine convex splitting time stepping with the neural solver for Allen-Cahn.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports error estimates, unconditional energy stability, and numerical experiments showing accurate layer resolution and better performance than finite elements on uniform meshes.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to 1D settings and relies on solving a non-convex optimization problem, so robustness may depend on initialization and extension to higher dimensions.
paper_title: Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations
